author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Measure sustained PS2 emulation performance instead of menu speed
summary: Define a ten-minute gameplay route, normalize battery, ambient conditions, power policy, and capture overhead, record interval timing from a cool start through steady temperature, and require two comparable runs.
heroAlt: PCSX2 on-screen performance statistics used to record sustained emulation timing

blocks.text: Replace the opening minute with a steady-state route

Menus and first rooms rarely represent a full play session. A useful sustained test includes the heaviest known gameplay, camera motion, effects, area transitions, and enough time for the phone to reach stable temperature. Define a route around ten minutes and specify when each segment begins so two runs can be compared at matching workload points.
Do not charge during one run and use battery during another, or record video in only one pass. Power and capture overhead can dominate the difference.
Normalize the device before each run

items: A fixed in-game route with minute-by-minute landmarks.
The same starting battery range and Android power mode.
Stable ambient temperature and case configuration.
Identical renderer, driver, profile, display brightness, and refresh rate.
A low-overhead timing method used in both runs.

blocks.text: Record the curve, not only the final average

items: 1. Let the phone return to a documented cool idle state and close unrelated workloads.
2. Cold-boot the title and start timing at the same in-game marker.
3. Record emulation speed, frame time, and visible stutter at regular route landmarks.
4. Note the first minute where performance stops changing materially or begins declining.
5. Complete the route without changing brightness, orientation, network load, or overlays.
6. Allow the device to return to the same starting condition.
7. Repeat the complete route with the identical profile.
8. Compare interval curves and reject an average that hides a late sustained drop.

blocks.text: A single average can combine a fast cool start with a slow hot finish. Interval evidence shows when the behavior changes and whether it aligns with a scene or with elapsed heat. Two runs reveal whether the curve is stable enough to guide settings.
The route is trustworthy when workload and timing curves repeat.

items: Both runs start from the same power and thermal conditions.
Landmark timing and input path remain comparable.
Late-session speed stays inside the chosen tolerance.
Audio cadence and frame pacing agree with numeric counters.
A profile labeled stable retains headroom at the heaviest segment.
A notification, download, or recording task interrupts one pass: rerun it.
Battery saver activates mid-route: normalize power policy.
Random game behavior changes workload: choose a more deterministic route.
The second run starts warm: wait for the documented baseline.

blocks.text: Restore normal brightness, network, and background-app behavior after recording the result, but keep the accepted per-game profile unchanged. Delete temporary overlays or logging settings that would add daily-play overhead.
A benchmark describes one device state

Ambient temperature, battery health, firmware, driver, and case can change sustained behavior later. Date the result and rerun after major Android or emulator updates. A five-minute peak is not interchangeable with a thirty-minute stable result: report warm-up, test duration, charge state, display brightness, and whether the phone was held or placed on a surface. Those conditions let a later run explain a real regression instead of mistaking a hotter room or different power policy for one.
